title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
overview: Ground language model answers in external documents by retrieving relevant passages at query time.
objectives: Explain chunking, embedding, and vector search

method.title: Indexing
method.body: Documents are split into chunks, embedded as vectors, and stored in an index.

method.title: Retrieval
method.body: The query is embedded and the nearest chunks, often by cosine similarity, are fetched.

method.title: Generation
method.body: Retrieved passages are placed in the prompt so the model can answer from them and cite sources.

method.title: Evaluation
method.body: Check whether the right passages were retrieved and whether the answer stays faithful to them.

pseudocode:
chunks = split(docs)
index = [(embed(c), c) for c in chunks]
q = embed(question)
top = sorted(index, key=lambda e: -cosine(q, e[0]))[:k]
answer = llm(question, context=top)

playground.starterCode:
import numpy as np
docs = {'cats': np.array([1.0, 0.1]), 'cars': np.array([0.1, 1.0])}
q = np.array([0.9, 0.2])
cos = lambda a, b: a @ b / (np.linalg.norm(a) * np.linalg.norm(b))
best = max(docs, key=lambda k: cos(q, docs[k]))
print('retrieved:', best)
